local_checks.invariant: mask_text masks well-formed credential shapes in every string payload value before persistence.
local_checks.result: A DSN inside a command ('psql postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd@db/app') was masked by _URL_CRED when the args were not truncated, and the human token is covered both by register_secret (api.py:86-88) and by the (agt|hum)_ token pattern (audit.py:69).

local_checks.invariant: Masking applies to the whole accepted argument blob, not to a pre-truncated prefix.
local_checks.result: Recon lead confirmed: _logged_args slices the JSON blob to 16,384 bytes and stores that head (service.py:189-194) before AuditLog._mask/mask_text ever runs (audit.py:160). With the same DSN ending exactly at the cut, the head ends with 'postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd', its '@' is dropped by the cut, _URL_CRED no longer matches, and the complete password survived masking into the append-only log; the identical untruncated command was masked. Partial tokens split at the cut (e.g. 'ghp_') also survive. Masking is an anti-accident control (a hostile agent can split any secret across values), so this is a hardening gap rather than a boundary failure.

local_checks.invariant: _mask covers every container a secret can sit in, including dict keys and non-str leaves.
local_checks.result: Recon lead confirmed: _mask recurses dict values and list items but returns keys unchanged (audit.py:137-147), so {'password=hunter2': 'v'} keeps the key verbatim. Every server-built payload uses fixed key names; only tool_request args carry agent-chosen keys (service.py:296), so the unmasked key is data the agent itself supplied and no human secret can reach a key. Hardening note only.

local_checks.invariant: Control-plane tokens are registered as secrets and never persist in the log in clear.
local_checks.result: The human token is registered before any append (api.py:86-88) and each sandbox token right after creation (service.py:436), and the token patterns in audit.py:58-70 additionally cover agt_/hum_ values of 16+ characters, so a token echoed into args, stdout_head or an error message is masked even if registration were missed.

local_checks.invariant: A failure inside the masking step cannot fall back to writing unmasked payloads or a broken chain.
local_checks.result: payload is masked at audit.py:160 before BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before the INSERT, and the hash is computed over the masked record (audit.py:169-184); an exception in masking aborts the append without a row, so there is no no-crypto fallback. The defect is only that such an exception is not converted to AuditWriteError (it escapes as a raw exception), which the unit-1 harness observed.

x_hardening: GET /audit applies min(limit, 5000) without a lower clamp (api.py:269); limit=-1 becomes SQL LIMIT -1 and returned the whole table in the local fixture. It is human-token only (api.py:126-129), so it is an operator self-cost; fix with max(1, min(limit, 5000)).

AuditLog.recent() runs COUNT(*) and a sandbox-filtered full scan (no index except the primary key, audit.py:23-34) inside the same lock that append() needs (audit.py:212-217, 158-186); /ui/audit is re-issued every 3 s per open page (templates/sandbox.html:19, web.py:265-269), so a large table lengthens a lock hold that blocks agent appends rather than failing fast.

approvals_view loads every historical approval row with full args/preview JSON twice (web.py:207-209) on a 2-second poll and keeps five, so approval retention multiplies control-plane memory and DB read work.

AgentBox.log_best_effort swallows AuditWriteError but lets other exceptions escape (service.py:366-372); the local harness showed a RuntimeError propagating after execution. AuditLog._mask iterates self._secrets without a lock while register_secret mutates it (audit.py:133-145) and raises before the try block, so that race becomes an unhandled 500 and a lost post-hoc record. Copy the set or guard it.

Masking runs after truncation: _logged_args cuts the blob to 16 KiB (service.py:189-194) and audit.py:160 masks only that head, so a complete credential whose delimiter falls past the cut persists (measured with postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd). Mask the full blob first, then truncate, and add a boundary regression fixture.

_mask rewrites values only, never dict keys (audit.py:137-147); the local fixture kept {'password=hunter2': ...} verbatim. Only tool_request args have agent-chosen keys today, so no human secret reaches a key, but masking keys costs nothing.

Approval rows are never deleted (not on decide, expire or sandbox delete; service.py:106-109, 471-475) although capture PNGs are, so the deleted-sandbox approval queue keeps raw args and previews forever in the same file.

decide() claims a row to 'approved' before snapshot and execution (approvals.py:82-89, service.py:395-418); a crash between claim and finish leaves it 'approved' forever because expire_stale only scans PENDING (service.py:379), so an agent can read a status for an action that never ran.

local_checks.result: bind_problem (cli.py:68-74) rejects any non-loopback host without TLS or --behind-tls-proxy, and the shipped Caddyfile terminates TLS and forwards to the container port that compose only exposes on the internal network (docker-compose.yml:29-30, 38-40). x_hardening: GET /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json and /healthz are served without any credential (all four returned 200 in the local check); /healthz also discloses runtime, image name, template names and dev_only (api.py:368-371). Build the app with docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None when not explicitly enabled, gate the schema routes, and reduce /healthz to {"ok": true} (api.py:111).

A non-ASCII credential turns secrets.compare_digest into a TypeError, so the JSON API answers a bare 500 instead of 401/403 (api.py:119) and both the agent approval attempt record (api.py:253-259) and the failed-login record (web.py:135-139) are skipped. Reject non-ASCII tokens before compare_digest, or compare bytes, so a malformed credential is a recorded 401.

Dependencies are declared as lower bounds only with no lockfile (pyproject.toml:8-18), so a rebuild can silently pick a different fastapi/uvicorn/starlette and with it different body-parsing and multipart defaults. Pin with hashes for reproducible deployments (the supply-chain block is out of scope for this run).

deploy/docker-compose.yml gives the control-plane container the Docker socket and sets no mem_limit/pids_limit, so both the body-buffering and the spool variants of the first candidate are bounded only by the host. Add container-level memory and pid limits and a sized tmpfs for /tmp as defence in depth.

The novnc extraction's success marker is a single file and the failure path is not recorded anywhere (sandbox_desktop.py:148-169), so an operator cannot tell a missing marker from a broken extraction. Log one audit row on extraction failure and expose the marker state on the desktop route instead of retrying silently.

agentbox/config.py:88-100: human_token() writes the new token and only then chmods it to 0600, so the admin secret is briefly created under the process umask; use os.open(..., 0o600) + os.fdopen, or mkstemp + rename. Same write-then-chmod shape at cli.py:157-159 (--env-file with the agent token).

agentbox/config.py:95-96 + agentbox/api.py:118-119: an existing human_token file that is empty or whitespace-only yields human_token()=='' and secrets.compare_digest('', '') then matches an 'Authorization: Bearer ' request as human. Reject tokens shorter than ~16 chars (fail closed) instead of trusting whatever the file contains.

agentbox/cli.py:340-341: the human-token refusal is a literal 'hum_' prefix test rather than a check of the credential class; config.py:90-92 never asserts that prefix on AGENTBOX_HUMAN_TOKEN, so the guard is bypassable by configuration. Compare against a kind returned by the server (e.g. a /whoami route) or refuse any token that authenticates as human.

agentbox/cli.py:47-53 (_check) prints the server's 'detail' string raw to the operator terminal; container-derived text can reach it through human CLI commands (ServiceError(400, str(e)) at service.py:362). Not a cross-principal boundary (the human already owns the token), but it is the one remaining unescaped terminal sink in cli.py and belongs to the h-webui escape_controls unit.

agentbox/cli.py:163-166 (cmd_list) prints s['source_dir'] without _safe. Settled negative for a cross-principal claim: POST /sandboxes is human_only (api.py:174-176), so only a human can choose that host path; no lower-trust principal can inject into it.

demo/injected_agent.py:41 forwards every AGENTBOX_* variable from the caller into the agent-side MCP subprocess, which includes AGENTBOX_HUMAN_TOKEN when the operator configures the token that way (config.py:88-92), contradicting the 'the human token never enters this code' invariant at agent.py:5; demo/run_demo.sh:81-85 also offers --auto y, which approves every pending request in a loop.
